race_context: The district: Southwest Parke Community School Corporation, based in Montezuma in Parke County, operated Montezuma Elementary, Rosedale Elementary and Riverton Parke Junior-Senior High School through 2025–26 {swp_july}. Beginning in 2026–27, all K–4 students attend Rosedale Elementary and grades 5–6 moved to Riverton Parke {swp_feed2}. Superintendent Philip T. Harrison, Ph.D., reported enrollment of 880 including preschool in August 2026, down from 1,015 in August 2025: 253 at Rosedale and 627 in grades 5–12 at Riverton Parke {swp_sept}.

The board has five members {swp_sept}. As of the September 2026 board packet they are Kevin Allen (president), Max Case (vice president), Daniel J. Harkrider (secretary), Nathan Adams and Tanner Edge {swp_sept}. The July 2026 packet listed Case as vice president and Harkrider as secretary, with Adams and Allen as members and no president {swp_july}. The ballot names numbered districts tied to townships (District 2 Wabash, District 3 Florida) plus an at-large District 5 {in_list}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three, one each for District 2 (Wabash), District 3 (Florida) and District 5 (At Large), each vote for one, matching the state list {in_list}. Nathan P. Adams, the only candidate for District 2, was elected to the board in 2022, according to state results, which do not name the district seat {sos_enr}. Board president Kevin Allen is running for the District 5 at-large seat against Lucas D. Collom {in_list}{swp_sept}.

Florida Township (District 3) seat: the board announced a vacancy effective July 1, 2026, with the appointee to serve through Dec. 31, 2026 {swp_feed1}. The board scheduled a July 23, 2026 special meeting to interview applicants, appoint a member and elect a board president {swp_feed1}{swp_july}. Tanner Edge first appears as a board member in the September 2026 packet; that he is the Florida appointee is an inference {swp_sept}. Edge is not on the ballot, so the District 3 race between Joshua T. Helton and Luke A. MacDonald will seat a new member {in_list}.

Montezuma Elementary closure (2026): on Feb. 10, 2026, the board voted 5–0 to close Montezuma Elementary, citing budget shortfalls; WTWO reported the school had 226 students who would go to Rosedale Elementary (317 students), 18.5 miles away {wtwo_close}{swp_feed2}. Parents quoted by WTWO said the item was added to the meeting with little notice and that the board had not run numbers on closing Rosedale instead; the superintendent had not responded to WTWO's request for comment {wtwo_close}. In his July 2026 report, Harrison said documents transferring Montezuma Elementary to Indiana Agriculture and Technology School (IATS) had been filed and recorded as of July 1, 2026 {swp_july}.

Charter school (2026): a group called United for Southwest Parke Schools worked with IATS on a charter school in Montezuma {ts_charter}. The University of Southern Indiana, a charter authorizer, held a public session in April 2026 on IATS's application for a K–6 charter school there; residents spoke in support and two Parke County superintendents raised concerns {ts_usi}.

Budget and cash flow (2026): Harrison reported that the enrollment drop of 135 students means an estimated $877,875.53 less in revenue, at state support of $7,768.81 per pupil {swp_sept}. The Operations Fund ended May 2026 at about –$755,474 and August 2026 at about –$166,115 in cash {swp_july}{swp_sept}. Harrison put the district on the interest list for the Indiana Bond Bank's Advance Funding Program (tax anticipation warrants), which he wrote could 'buy us some additional time to make more reductions as needed to fully align our expenses and revenue' {swp_sept}. Hearings on the 2027 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan were held Sept. 9, 2026, with budget adoption set for Oct. 21, 2026 {swp_sept}.

Referendum (2025): on May 6, 2025, voters rejected a proposal for up to $10 million in bonds or a lease over 22 years to build an auxiliary gym at Riverton Parke Junior-Senior High School, 762 to 392 {wtwo_ref}.

Other 2026 items: the board took up a personal communication devices policy (5136R) on second reading in July 2026 {swp_july}, and in spring 2026 the district surveyed families on possible changes to the elementary school's name, colors and mascot {swp_feed2}.
Forums: no candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the 2026 Southwest Parke races was found.
